text.p: These are the leading stories in Zambia's newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- World Bank representative Gedion Nkojo said the institution was pleased with Zambia's economic programme, which is considered well thought-out. He was speaking when he visited government officials in the Northern province on Tuesday.
- The state-run Zambia National Commercial Bank has laid off 1,000 workers in a programme to rationalise operations.
- Workers in the central town of Kabwe went on strike on Tuesday, locking up offices and vandalising the mayor's vehicle.
- The Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa charged on Tuesday that non-African economic blocs are weakening it by encouraging weaker members to withdraw from the grouping.

- Eight opposition politicians detained last year for alleged treason have sued the state for wrongful and malicious prosecution and are demanding damages. The eight are all members of former president Kenneth Kaunda's United National Independence Paty (UNIP).
